A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MeG research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A.1–A.13 support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original knowledge-editing experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations and efficiency measurements, including appendix results on UnKEBench and MQuAKE-CF.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results throughout the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The contrastively tuned text encoder, familiarity network, diffusion weight generator and dynamic single-neuron attachment remain unchanged. The appendix adaptations and inference procedure are also retained.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ZsRE, COUNTERFACT, BBH, GSM8K, MMLU, RTE, SST-2, UnKEBench and MQuAKE-CF. The newly cited RouterEval and MiniLongBench works do not introduce evaluated datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments: FT, MEMIT, PMET, MALMEN and SCEN retain their existing comparisons; Table 18 retains MEMIT/MALMEN and Table 19 retains AlphaEdit. RLEdit remains discussed without an experimental comparison.

E3.justification: Model configurations, editing scales, AG/TF evaluation, metrics, preprocessing and benchmark-specific protocols are unchanged. The training settings and baseline reproduction procedures in Appendices A.11–A.12 are also retained.

E4.justification: Both retain the encoder and familiarity-network ablations, DiT-versus-MLP comparison, diffusion-step sensitivity, data augmentation, layer selection, entropy-threshold analysis, neuron-capacity tests and causal tracing. Relocated displays contain the same analyses.

E5.justification: Section 9 in both versions states that experiments are averaged over five independent runs with fixed random seeds. No run-count revision, new uncertainty reporting or statistical test is introduced.

E6.justification: Results in Tables 1–21 and Figures 3–8 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains MeG's Phi-2/ZsRE 10,000-edit Score of 82.80, and Table 18 retains its MQuAKE-CF multi-hop result of 41.41.

T1.justification: Section 3's mathematical definitions and Section 4's objectives, entropy routing and diffusion/inference equations are unchanged. No formal assumption, theorem, proof or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about dynamic single-neuron editing, scalability, interference control and overall editing performance. The added code-access sentence does not revise the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of locality preservation, generality/efficiency trade-offs, neuron capacity and competing methods' limitations are retained. No substantive interpretation, applicability boundary or limitation is added.

D1.justification: v4 adds a MeG code-repository address in the abstract, providing access information absent from v1. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing and prompts are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Huang et al.'s RouterEval and MiniLongBench references to the introduction's general LLM background. The related-work discussion, novelty positioning and relationships to knowledge-editing methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 updates the author/contact block and corresponding-author designation, corrects the Appendix A.8 heading and Table 22 wording, and makes isolated wording edits. It also introduces 'Reliablity' in the abstract; the narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 colors citation and cross-reference links and adjusts wrapping and display placement. Table 19 moves from page 22 to 23, Table 23 from 26 to 27, and Figure 8 from 27 to 28; the figures and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: The new code-repository pointer in v4's abstract modestly improves reproducibility documentation. Wording and layout edits have mixed minor effects, including a new abstract typo, while the scientific evidence remains unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the linked code's completeness or usability.
